name: SN 441011 (Type J, Swiss T12/T13 and T23)
description: Swiss household plug and socket system: two pins 19 mm apart with a central earth pin offset by 5 mm, which polarises the connection. The 10 A series (T12 plug, T13 socket) has round pins; the 16 A series (T23) has rectangular pins. Sockets are hierarchically downward compatible: a 16 A socket also takes 10 A plugs.

variants.name: Type 12 plug (10 A)
variants.keying: The offset earth pin enforces polarity.
mechanicalNotes: Round pins 4 mm in diameter, 19 mm long; line and neutral 19 mm apart, earth offset 5 mm from their line.
Line and neutral pins partially insulated (8 mm) on current plugs.

variants.name: Type 13 socket-outlet (10 A)
variants.keying: Offset earth hole: the plug enters one way only.
mechanicalNotes: Recessed socket; the line and neutral contacts sit deeper than the earth contact, so earth makes first.
Also made as a triple socket-outlet.

notes: Ratings and dimensions rely on secondary sources citing SEV 1011:2009; the SN 441011 parts were not reviewed.
Line on the right looking into a T13 socket with the earth hole down relies on a single secondary source (Wikipedia); the drawing follows it.
The Type 13 socket also accepts the Europlug (Type C, CEE 7/16); the mating is stored on the 'europlug' family.
Unearthed plugs (T11, T21), the obsolete flush T12 socket and the three-phase T15/T25 types are not modelled.
IEC 60906-1 (Type N) derives from this design but is not compatible: reversed polarity and a 3 mm earth offset.
